english_retrieval.title: Akshaya Tritiya - Wikipedia
english_retrieval.snippet: Annual Hindu and Jain festival. Many Jainas and Hindus consider the day auspicious for those who buy rice, deposit money in a bank account, buy any kind of new things or vessels, visit temples, donate food to the poor, or help the poor with fees for their education.*[citation needed*]. Akshay Tritiya is considered one of the most auspicious days in both the Hindu and Jain religious calendars, distinguised from other festivals by the belief, worship, fasting, or the commencement of a new venture - generates inexhaustible spiritual merit that never diminishes. In Jainism's Śvetāmbara tradition, devotees break their 400-days-long fast with eating only on alternate days, that is meant to replicate Ṛṣabhanātha's 400-days-long fast partially. The festival is so named because it falls on the third lunar day (tṛtīyā) of the spring month of Vaiśākha in the Hindu calendar. In Jainism, Akshaya Tritiya is an important festival, as it commemorates the first Tirthankara, Rishabhanatha, ending a 400-day-long fast by consuming sugarcane juice poured into his cupped hands.

merged_results.title: Akshaya Tritiya - Wikipedia
merged_results.snippet: Annual Hindu and Jain festival. Many Jainas and Hindus consider the day auspicious for those who buy rice, deposit money in a bank account, buy any kind of new things or vessels, visit temples, donate food to the poor, or help the poor with fees for their education.*[citation needed*]. Akshay Tritiya is considered one of the most auspicious days in both the Hindu and Jain religious calendars, distinguised from other festivals by the belief, worship, fasting, or the commencement of a new venture - generates inexhaustible spiritual merit that never diminishes. In Jainism's Śvetāmbara tradition, devotees break their 400-days-long fast with eating only on alternate days, that is meant to replicate Ṛṣabhanātha's 400-days-long fast partially. The festival is so named because it falls on the third lunar day (tṛtīyā) of the spring month of Vaiśākha in the Hindu calendar. In Jainism, Akshaya Tritiya is an important festival, as it commemorates the first Tirthankara, Rishabhanatha, ending a 400-day-long fast by consuming sugarcane juice poured into his cupped hands.
